packageRules.description: Playwright's npm package and its container image must move in the same pull request. The image ships the browser binaries built for that exact release, so letting them move apart would leave the suite comparing screenshots against baselines captured by a different renderer. No preset can know this, which is why it is written here.
prBodyNotes: :warning: After merging, regenerate the visual baselines with `npm run docker:vr:update` and commit them. A browser update moves glyph rendering, so the committed baselines will no longer match.
Regenerate the agent definitions with `npx playwright init-agents --loop=claude`, then re-append the project rules section each one ends with. They are generated from the installed version.
Check that the Dockerfile tags in `env/docker/` and the version in `package.json` name the same release.

packageRules.description: The Allure reporter and its command line generator have to agree on the results format, so they are reviewed together.
Workflow actions, grouped to keep the pipeline's own updates in one review. Node 20 leaving the runners is exactly the kind of change that arrives this way.

Linters and formatters merge themselves once the gate is green, on non major updates only. Renovate's automerge guidance names development dependencies, and linters and formatters in particular, as the safest category, and limits the practice to non major updates. Nothing here changes what the application does, and the pipeline still has to pass first.

Playwright is never automerged. A version change moves glyph rendering, so it needs the baselines regenerated and the agent definitions rebuilt before it can be believed. This is exactly the case Renovate's guidance describes as one to read before merging.
